156	' Optional feature: reads a manager-maintained per-unit leave/duty roster. Each unit
157	' pastes its own roster into its own table on the "Roster" sheet (named tblRoster_<Unit>,
158	' e.g. tblRoster_PSO) -- LoadRoster discovers every table whose name starts with
159	' "tblRoster" and merges them all into one combined rosterData dictionary, so units can
160	' be added/removed/resized independently without any VBA change. Matching is by plain
161	' day-of-month (1-31), not calendar date -- the native rosters this feature reads from
162	' have no month/year anywhere in them, only a day-number column per day. tblRosterCodes
163	' (Config sheet) lists the recognized leave codes. Both are optional -- if the Roster
164	' sheet is absent, or has no tblRoster* tables, this leaves rosterCodes/rosterData empty
165	' and every [-] day behaves exactly as it does without this feature (see
166	' ReportBuilder.BuildDepartmentSheets, Case "NOPUNCH").
167	' rosterData is keyed "UCASE(TRIM(AttendanceName))|DayOfMonth" -> UCase'd code string.
168	Public Sub LoadRoster(wb As Workbook, ByRef rosterCodes As Object, ByRef rosterData As Object)
169	    Set rosterCodes = CreateObject("Scripting.Dictionary")
170	    Set rosterData = CreateObject("Scripting.Dictionary")
171	    Set RosterWarnings = New Collection
172	
173	    On Error GoTo UnexpectedError
174	
175	    LastAction = "LoadRoster: locating tblRosterCodes"
176	    Dim cfgWs As Worksheet
177	    Set cfgWs = wb.Sheets("Config")
178	    Dim lo As ListObject, codesTbl As ListObject
179	    For Each lo In cfgWs.ListObjects
180	        If lo.Name = "tblRosterCodes" Then Set codesTbl = lo: Exit For
181	    Next lo
182	
183	    If Not codesTbl Is Nothing Then
184	        Dim ci As Long, codeVal As String
185	        For ci = 1 To codesTbl.ListRows.Count
186	            LastAction = "LoadRoster: reading tblRosterCodes row " & ci
187	            codeVal = UCase(Trim(CStr(codesTbl.DataBodyRange(ci, 1).Value)))
188	            If codeVal <> "" Then rosterCodes(codeVal) = True
189	        Next ci
190	    End If
191	
192	    LastAction = "LoadRoster: locating Roster sheet"
193	    Dim sh As Worksheet, rosterWs As Worksheet
194	    For Each sh In wb.Sheets
195	        If sh.Name = "Roster" Then Set rosterWs = sh: Exit For
196	    Next sh
197	    If rosterWs Is Nothing Then Exit Sub
198	
199	    Dim seenNames As Object
200	    Set seenNames = CreateObject("Scripting.Dictionary")
201	
202	    Dim rosterTbl As ListObject
203	    LastAction = "LoadRoster: enumerating tblRoster* tables"
204	    For Each lo In rosterWs.ListObjects
205	        If UCase(Left(lo.Name, 9)) <> "TBLROSTER" Then GoTo NextTable
206	        Set rosterTbl = lo
207	
208	        LastAction = "LoadRoster: locating Attendance Name column in " & rosterTbl.Name
209	        Dim nameCol As ListColumn, idCol As Long
210	        idCol = 0
211	        For Each nameCol In rosterTbl.ListColumns
212	            If nameCol.Name = "Attendance Name" Then idCol = nameCol.Index: Exit For
213	        Next nameCol
214	        If idCol = 0 Then
215	            RosterWarnings.Add rosterTbl.Name & " is missing an 'Attendance Name' column -- roster matching skipped for this table."
216	            GoTo NextTable
217	        End If
218	
219	        LastAction = "LoadRoster: discovering day-of-month columns in " & rosterTbl.Name
220	        Dim dayColIdx() As Long, dayOfMonthVal() As Long, nDayCols As Long
221	        ReDim dayColIdx(1 To rosterTbl.ListColumns.Count)
222	        ReDim dayOfMonthVal(1 To rosterTbl.ListColumns.Count)
223	        nDayCols = 0
224	
225	        Dim seenDays As Object
226	        Set seenDays = CreateObject("Scripting.Dictionary")
227	
228	        Dim lc As ListColumn, hdrVal As Variant, dayNum As Long
229	        For Each lc In rosterTbl.ListColumns
230	            hdrVal = lc.Range.Cells(1, 1).Value
231	            If IsNumeric(hdrVal) Then
232	                dayNum = CLng(hdrVal)
233	                If dayNum >= 1 And dayNum <= 31 Then
234	                    If seenDays.Exists(dayNum) Then
235	                        RosterWarnings.Add rosterTbl.Name & " has a duplicate day-of-month column (" & _
236	                            dayNum & ") -- first occurrence used."
237	                    Else
238	                        seenDays(dayNum) = True
239	                        nDayCols = nDayCols + 1
240	                        dayColIdx(nDayCols) = lc.Index
241	                        dayOfMonthVal(nDayCols) = dayNum
242	                    End If
243	                End If
244	            End If
245	        Next lc
246	
247	        LastAction = "LoadRoster: reading " & rosterTbl.Name & " rows"
248	        Dim ri As Long, empName As String
249	        For ri = 1 To rosterTbl.ListRows.Count
250	            LastAction = "LoadRoster: reading " & rosterTbl.Name & " row " & ri
251	            empName = UCase(Trim(CStr(rosterTbl.DataBodyRange(ri, idCol).Value)))
252	            If empName = "" Then GoTo NextRosterRow
253	
254	            If seenNames.Exists(empName) Then
255	                RosterWarnings.Add rosterTbl.Name & " has a duplicate Attendance Name (" & empName & ") -- first occurrence used."
256	                GoTo NextRosterRow
257	            End If
258	            seenNames(empName) = True
259	
260	            Dim di As Long, cellVal As String
261	            For di = 1 To nDayCols
262	                cellVal = UCase(Trim(CStr(rosterTbl.DataBodyRange(ri, dayColIdx(di)).Value)))
263	                If cellVal <> "" Then rosterData(empName & "|" & dayOfMonthVal(di)) = cellVal
264	            Next di
265	NextRosterRow:
266	        Next ri
267	NextTable:
268	    Next lo
269	    Exit Sub
270	
271	UnexpectedError:
272	    RosterWarnings.Add "Unexpected error while loading Roster data (" & Err.Description & _
273	        ") -- roster matching skipped for this run."
274	    Set rosterCodes = CreateObject("Scripting.Dictionary")
275	    Set rosterData = CreateObject("Scripting.Dictionary")
276	End Sub

228	            Dim effectiveIn As Double

4	' Raw cell formats observed in the Monthly Punch List export:
5	'   "07:47-17:00"  -> normal, both punches present
6	'   "[-]"          -> scheduled day, zero punches at all
7	'   "09:27-]"      -> clock-in present, clock-out missing
8	'   "[-17:01"      -> clock-in missing, clock-out present
9	'   ""             -> not scheduled that day (blank cell, not an error)
10	' Returns one of: "NORMAL","NOPUNCH","MISSING_IN","MISSING_OUT","BLANK","UNKNOWN"
11	Public Function ParsePunchCell(raw As String, ByRef hasIn As Boolean, ByRef hasOut As Boolean, _
12	                                ByRef inTime As Double, ByRef outTime As Double) As String
13	    Dim s As String
14	    s = Trim(raw)
15	    hasIn = False
16	    hasOut = False
17	    inTime = 0
18	    outTime = 0
19	
20	    If s = "" Then
21	        ParsePunchCell = "BLANK"
22	        Exit Function
23	    End If
24	
25	    If s = "[-]" Then
26	        ParsePunchCell = "NOPUNCH"
27	        Exit Function
28	    End If
29	
30	    Dim dashPos As Long
31	    dashPos = InStr(s, "-")
32	    If dashPos = 0 Then
33	        ParsePunchCell = "UNKNOWN"
34	        Exit Function
35	    End If
36	
37	    Dim leftPart As String, rightPart As String
38	    leftPart = Trim(Left(s, dashPos - 1))
39	    rightPart = Trim(Mid(s, dashPos + 1))
40	
41	    If leftPart = "[" Then
42	        hasIn = False
43	    Else
44	        hasIn = True
45	        On Error GoTo BadFormat
46	        inTime = TimeSerial(CInt(Left(leftPart, 2)), CInt(Mid(leftPart, 4, 2)), 0)
47	        On Error GoTo 0
48	    End If
49	
50	    If rightPart = "]" Then
51	        hasOut = False
52	    Else
53	        hasOut = True
54	        On Error GoTo BadFormat
55	        outTime = TimeSerial(CInt(Left(rightPart, 2)), CInt(Mid(rightPart, 4, 2)), 0)
56	        On Error GoTo 0
57	    End If
58	
59	    If hasIn And hasOut Then
60	        ParsePunchCell = "NORMAL"
61	    ElseIf hasIn And Not hasOut Then
62	        ParsePunchCell = "MISSING_OUT"
63	    ElseIf Not hasIn And hasOut Then
64	        ParsePunchCell = "MISSING_IN"
65	    Else
66	        ParsePunchCell = "NOPUNCH"
67	    End If
68	    Exit Function
69	
70	BadFormat:
71	    ParsePunchCell = "UNKNOWN"
72	End Function

1	# Roster/Leave Ingestion — Auto-Resolve NO PUNCH Days — Design Spec
2	
3	Date: 2026-07-07
4	
5	> **Partially superseded (2026-07-08):** the "Clock-In Status is never changed" rule below
6	> was revised. A roster-confirmed `[-]` day now DOES change `Clock-In Status` to
7	> `NO PUNCH - ROSTER: <code>` with a light-blue row color, and the summary block gained a
8	> `Roster-Resolved` column. See `CLAUDE.md` "Key invariants", `Attendance_Analyzer_Context.md`,
9	> and `2026-07-08-ttsh-wide-adoption-design.md`. Everything else in this spec stands.
10	
11	## Purpose
12	
13	Today, any `[-]` ("no punch captured") day is always flagged `NO PUNCH - VERIFY` with a
14	blank Verification dropdown, left entirely to manual tagging — because no leave data was
15	available when the tool was built, and auto-classifying a guess was explicitly rejected
16	(`Attendance_Analyzer_Context.md`, `CLAUDE.md` "Key invariants").
17	
18	Every unit already keeps its own monthly roster (a manager-maintained Excel grid: one row
19	per staff, one column per day, cells mixing duty-rotation codes like `C1`/`FC`/`CH Ref`
20	with leave codes like `AL`/`MC`/`FCL`) as their leave/MC record of truth. This spec adds a
21	path for that roster data to reach the analyzer, so a `[-]` day that the roster confirms
22	as leave gets pre-filled instead of left fully manual — while a `[-]` day the roster
23	doesn't explain (or that a unit hasn't set up a roster for at all) behaves exactly as it
24	does today.
25	
26	This is not a file importer for units' native roster workbooks (format varies per unit,
27	first-name-only identification, monthly tab layout that would need a fragile per-unit
28	parser). Instead, managers copy their roster into a small standardized table inside
29	`Attendance_Analyzer.xlsx` itself, using the same "Config sheet, Excel Table, no VBA
30	change needed" pattern `tblSchedule`/`tblVerification` already establish. No Employee ID
31	lookups are required — the table carries its own name-to-name mapping (below), so
32	managers work entirely with names they already recognize.
33	
34	## New data: Roster sheet + `tblRoster` table
35	
36	A new sheet, **"Roster"**, in `Attendance_Analyzer.xlsx`, holding one Excel Table,
37	**`tblRoster`**:
38	
39	| Attendance Name | Roster Name | 1-May-2026 | 2-May-2026 | ... |
40	|---|---|---|---|---|
41	| Fieda Binte Ahmad | Fieda | AL | | ... |
42	| Sylvia Tan Wei Ling | Sylvia | | MC | ... |
43	
44	- **Attendance Name** — the employee's name exactly as it appears in the raw punch
45	  export/output (i.e. matching `fName` in `ReportBuilder.BuildDepartmentSheets`, built as
46	  `Trim(FirstName & " " & LastName)`). **This is the join key** used to match a `[-]` day
47	  to a roster row — not Employee ID.
48	- **Roster Name** — the name as it appears in the unit's own native monthly roster (often
49	  just a first name, e.g. `"Fieda"`). Informational only, not used in matching — it exists
50	  so a manager copying data in can visually cross-reference which row of `tblRoster`
51	  corresponds to which row of their native roster while pasting in that row's codes. This
52	  is the two-column mapping that replaces needing an Employee ID at all: the manager
53	  writes the one name they may not immediately recognize (`Attendance Name`, looked up
54	  once against the punch export or output sheet) next to the name they already know
55	  (`Roster Name`, straight from their native roster).
56	- **Date columns** — real calendar dates (entered as actual Excel date values, not
57	  weekday names or text), one column per day that has at least one relevant code to
58	  record. Because matching is by literal date rather than by fixed column position or
59	  weekday, the table doesn't need to be resized or relaid-out for month length —
60	  managers can either replace the table's date columns each month or keep appending new
61	  ones over time; both work identically since date columns are discovered dynamically
62	  (see below), not hardcoded to a fixed range.
63	- A cell is left blank for any day with nothing worth recording (normal working day, or a
64	  duty/rotation code the analyzer doesn't care about — see next section).
65	- Matching on `Attendance Name` is case-insensitive and trimmed (names are more prone to
66	  casing/whitespace slips than an ID would be), but otherwise an exact string match — a
67	  name that doesn't match exactly (typo, missing middle name, nickname vs legal name)
68	  simply doesn't resolve, same safe fallback as any other non-match.
69	
70	## New Config table: `tblRosterCodes`
71	
72	A new small table in the existing **Config** sheet, **`tblRosterCodes`**, single column
73	`Code`, listing the exact codes recognized as leave, regardless of department:
74	
75	```
76	AL
77	MC
78	OIL
79	FCL
80	PH
81	SLWOMC
82	UL
83	BL
84	```
85	
86	This list is Config-driven (not a hardcoded VBA constant) so adding a 9th code later is a
87	Config edit only, consistent with how `tblSchedule`/`tblVerification` already work — no
88	VBA change, no re-import.
89	
90	Matching against this list is **exact match only** (case-insensitive, trimmed) — a cell
91	value has to equal one of these codes exactly. Variants that aren't exact matches (e.g.
92	`AL(PM)`, `AL (PN)`, `MC/AL`, `UFCL`) do **not** match and are treated the same as any
93	other unrecognized code: the day stays `NO PUNCH - VERIFY`, unaffected. Duty/rotation
94	codes (`A`, `O`, `T`, `C1`, `C2`, `FC`, `CH Ref`, `Ref`, `Standby`, `Course`, etc.) are
95	never in this list and are always ignored by this feature.
96	
97	## `tblVerification` extension
98	
99	The same 8 codes are added as 8 new rows in the existing `tblVerification` table,
100	alongside the current 6 generic options (`Approved Leave`, `MC (Medical Certificate)`,
101	`Off-Roster Change`, `Genuine Absence`, `Forgot to Punch (Whole Day)`,
102	`Other - see notes`). This makes them valid values in the Verification dropdown for
103	manual selection too, and is what the auto-fill (below) writes into that column.
104	
105	`tblRosterCodes` (what the matcher checks against) and `tblVerification`'s list (what's
106	selectable in the dropdown) are two separate tables kept in sync by content, not by
107	formula reference — same independence `tblSchedule` and `tblVerification` already have
108	from each other.
109	
110	## Processing change: `BuildDepartmentSheets`, `Case "NOPUNCH"`
111	
112	Currently (`ReportBuilder.bas`, around line 226):
113	```vba
114	Case "NOPUNCH"
115	    statusIn = "NO PUNCH - VERIFY"
116	    statusOut = "N/A"
117	```
118	No Verification value is written; the cell is left for manual dropdown selection.
119	
120	New behavior, same branch:
121	1. Look up `UCase(Trim(fName)) & "|" & CLng(theDaysDate)` in the in-memory roster
122	   dictionary (built by the new loader, below), where `fName` is the same
123	   `Trim(FirstName & " " & LastName)` value already computed earlier in
124	   `BuildDepartmentSheets` for this row.
125	2. If found, and the stored code is (case-insensitively, trimmed) an exact match to one of
126	   `tblRosterCodes`, write that code into the Verification column (Q) for this row.
127	3. Otherwise — no roster entry for this employee's name, no date column for this day,
128	   roster data unavailable this run, or a code present but not in `tblRosterCodes` —
129	   behavior is completely unchanged from today: Verification stays blank, `Clock-In
130	   Status` still reads `NO PUNCH - VERIFY`.
131	
132	~~`Clock-In Status` is **never** changed by this feature — the row stays visually flagged
133	(still gets `ApplyRowColor`'s purple highlight) either way. Only the Verification cell
134	gets pre-filled when there's a confirmed match.~~ *(Superseded 2026-07-08 — see note at
135	top: a confirmed match now changes `Clock-In Status` and the row color.)* No other `Case`
136	branch (`NORMAL`, `MISSING_IN`, `MISSING_OUT`, `BLANK`, `UNKNOWN`) is touched by this
137	feature at all.
138	
139	## New loader
140	
141	A new `LoadRoster` routine (in `Helpers.bas`, alongside `LoadConfig`) reads `tblRoster` +
142	`tblRosterCodes` into:
143	- `rosterCodes As Object` (`Scripting.Dictionary`, the 8 recognized codes, UCase-keyed, for
144	  O(1) membership checks)
145	- `rosterData As Object` (`Scripting.Dictionary`, keyed
146	  `UCase(Trim(AttendanceName)) & "|" & CLng(dateSerial)` → raw code string)
147	
148	Date columns in `tblRoster` are discovered the same way `PunchParser.ParseDayHeaders`
149	already discovers date columns in the raw punch export: scan the header row, keep only
150	columns where `IsDate(header) = True`, skip anything else silently (see error handling
151	below) rather than assuming a fixed column count or position.
152	
153	`MainMacro.GenerateAttendanceReport` calls `LoadRoster` once, right after `LoadConfig`,
154	passing the results into `BuildDepartmentSheets` alongside the existing `schedule` and
155	`verifyOptions` parameters.
156	
157	## Error handling & validation
158	
159	**Roster-specific, all non-blocking** (a broken or absent Roster setup must never stop
160	report generation for departments that don't use it):
161	
162	- **"Roster" sheet or `tblRoster` missing entirely** → not an error. Treated as "not
163	  adopted yet" — `rosterData` stays empty, every `[-]` day behaves exactly as today.
164	- **`tblRoster` missing its `Attendance Name` column** → Roster matching is skipped for
165	  the entire run (not per-row), with one warning recorded (see Surfacing, below).
166	- **Invalid/non-date column header in `tblRoster`** → that column is silently skipped,
167	  same self-adjusting behavior `ParseDayHeaders` already has — no warning, no error (this
168	  mirrors how the punch list export already tolerates non-date columns).
169	- **Duplicate Attendance Name rows** in `tblRoster` (case-insensitive) → first occurrence
170	  wins; the duplicate name is added to the warnings list.
171	- **Duplicate date columns** (two columns resolving to the same calendar date) → same
172	  treatment: first occurrence wins, warning recorded.
173	- **`tblRosterCodes` missing** → treated as an empty list (no codes recognized); every
174	  `[-]` day behaves exactly as today. Not an error, since this table is only meaningful
175	  together with `tblRoster`.
176	- **Any unexpected error while reading the Roster sheet** (e.g. corrupted table) is caught
177	  inside `LoadRoster` itself, not propagated to `MainMacro`'s top-level `ErrHandler` —
178	  falls back to "no roster data" behavior for the whole run, with a warning recorded.
179	
180	**Surfacing:** warnings collected during `LoadRoster` are appended to the existing
181	completion `MsgBox` in `MainMacro.bas` (the one that already reads "Attendance report
182	generated... check purple rows") as an additional paragraph, rather than interrupting
183	mid-run — consistent with the existing "run once, inspect by eye afterward" workflow.
184	
185	**General hardening pass (existing code, found while designing this feature):**
186	
187	`Helpers.LoadConfig` currently has several unguarded operations that would surface as
188	generic, hard-to-diagnose VBA runtime errors (still caught by `MainMacro`'s top-level
189	`ErrHandler` today, so nothing crashes silently or corrupts output — but the message
190	doesn't say what actually went wrong):
191	
192	- `cfgWs.Range("GracePeriod").Value` (line 34) — throws a generic error if the named range
193	  is missing or renamed. Add an existence check first; raise a named error
194	  (`"GracePeriod named range not found in Config sheet"`) if absent.
195	- `cfgWs.ListObjects("tblSchedule")` / `"tblVerification"` (lines 43, 66) — same treatment:
196	  check existence first, raise a named error identifying which table is missing.
197	- `CDbl(tbl.DataBodyRange(i, 4).Value)` / `(i, 5)` (lines 56-57) — throws a generic Type
198	  Mismatch if a Start/End Time cell has non-numeric content, with no indication of which
199	  row. Guard with `IsNumeric` first; if it fails, raise a named error including the
200	  department and weekday of the offending row (`"tblSchedule row for PSO/Saturday has a
201	  non-numeric Start Time"`).
202	- Add `LastAction` updates inside the `tblSchedule`/`tblVerification` loops (e.g.
203	  `"LoadConfig: reading tblSchedule row 5 (dept=PSO, weekday=Saturday)"`), matching the
204	  per-row granularity `BuildDepartmentSheets` already has, so a failure's `MsgBox`
205	  (`MainMacro.bas` line ~79, `"Last action: " & LastAction`) points at the exact row
206	  instead of just "Loading Config sheet."
207	- The new `LoadRoster` code follows this same hardened pattern from the start (named
208	  errors, per-row `LastAction`), for consistency with the rest of the codebase.
209	
210	This doesn't add a new error-handling layer or change the single-top-level-`ErrHandler`
211	architecture — it makes the messages that already reach that handler specific and
212	actionable instead of generic.
213	
214	## Out of scope
215	
216	- No per-department code vocabulary or code-to-category translation table. The 8-code
217	  list in `tblRosterCodes` is global and department-agnostic, per the "streamlined list,
218	  duty codes never matter" decision.
219	- No fuzzy/substring/prefix matching for code variants (`AL(PM)`, `MC/AL`, `UFCL`, etc.) —

1	# Roster Sheet — One Table Per Unit, Day-of-Month Matching — Design Spec
2	
3	Date: 2026-07-07
4	
5	**Amends** `2026-07-07-roster-leave-ingestion-design.md`: that spec's matching mechanism
6	(exact calendar date, discovered via `IsDate()` on column headers) is superseded by the
7	day-of-month mechanism below, based on a real sample of a unit's native roster. Everything
8	else in that spec (join key = `Attendance Name`, `tblRosterCodes`, exact-match-only,
9	`Case "NOPUNCH"` writing to the Verification column, graceful non-blocking degradation)
10	is unchanged.
11	
12	## Purpose
13	
14	The Roster sheet (added in `2026-07-07-roster-leave-ingestion-design.md`) currently holds
15	one shared `tblRoster` table (`Attendance Name` | `Roster Name` | date columns) that every
16	unit's rows get typed into together. In practice, each unit already keeps its own native
17	monthly roster (a name column plus one column per day-of-month), and a manager wants to
18	paste their whole unit's roster data into the tool in one action rather than retyping rows
19	into a table shared with other units.
20	
21	This spec splits `tblRoster` into one table per unit (department), stacked vertically on
22	the Roster sheet, and changes how a day gets matched: from an exact calendar date to a
23	plain day-of-month number, matching how the native rosters actually look.
24	
25	## What the native roster actually looks like (confirmed from a real sample)
26	
27	A unit's native roster is a grid: one row per employee, one column per **day-of-month**
28	(`1`-`31`, plain numbers — not real dates, no month or year anywhere in the file), cells
29	holding a mix of duty/rotation codes (`CH Ref`, `C1`, `C2`, `FC`, `RD`, ...) and leave
30	codes (`AL`, `CCL`, ...), plus trailing summary rows (`Actual Man Day`, `Max Headcount...`)
31	that aren't employee data at all.
32	
33	This changes two things from the original spec:
34	
35	1. **No calendar date exists anywhere in the source data.** Matching by exact date
36	   (`IsDate()` on headers, keyed by `CLng(dateSerial)`) cannot work against data pasted
37	   from this format — every header would be a plain integer `1`-`31`, and while VBA's
38	   `IsDate()` technically accepts a bare number (treating it as an OLE date serial), that
39	   resolves to a nonsense date near the 1899/1900 epoch, not "the Nth day of this month."
40	   Silently wrong, not silently absent — the failure mode this spec exists to avoid.
41	2. **Summary rows aren't a special case to filter out.** `Actual Man Day` / `Max
42	   Headcount...` (and any other non-employee row) simply never match an `Attendance Name`
43	   in the punch export, so they're inert by the same "no match = no-op" rule that already
44	   applies to any other non-matching name — no extra filtering logic needed.
45	
46	## Matching mechanism: day-of-month, not calendar date
47	
48	`tblRoster_X` tables key their date columns by **plain day-of-month number** (`1`-`31`),
49	not by calendar date. Since nothing in the roster ever states which month it's for,
50	matching assumes the roster's currently-pasted data reflects whichever month the Monthly
51	Punch List being processed covers — consistent with the "replace monthly" refresh model
52	below (at any moment, the roster only ever holds one month's data).
53	
54	- `rosterData` is now keyed `UCase(Trim(AttendanceName)) & "|" & dayOfMonth` (`dayOfMonth`
55	  a plain `Long`, `1`-`31`), not by date serial.
56	- `Helpers.LoadRoster`'s column discovery changes from `IsDate(hdrVal)` to a numeric check:
57	  a header counts as a day column only if it's numeric and in `1`-`31`
58	  (`IsNumeric(hdrVal) And CLng(hdrVal) >= 1 And CLng(hdrVal) <= 31`) — rejects blank
59	  headers, text headers, and out-of-range numbers, not just non-dates.
60	- `ReportBuilder.BuildDepartmentSheets`'s `Case "NOPUNCH"` branch builds its lookup key
61	  from `Day(dayDates(d))` (the day-of-month component of the punch list's actual date for
62	  that column) instead of `CLng(dayDates(d))` (the full date serial). This is the one
63	  change to `ReportBuilder.bas` this spec requires — everything else in that file is
64	  unaffected.
65	
66	**Known limitation, accepted as-is**: if a roster is stale (still showing last month's
67	codes when this month's punch list is processed), a day-of-month match could pull the
68	wrong month's code for that day. This is the same trust placed in "replace monthly" as a
69	process discipline already, not a new risk introduced by this change — there is no way to
70	detect staleness without a month/year somewhere in the source data, which the native
71	format doesn't have.
72	
73	## Table setup: static headers, monthly data-only refresh
74	
75	Each `tblRoster_X` table's headers are **static and set up once**:
76	`Attendance Name | Roster Name | 1 | 2 | 3 | ... | 31` (33 columns total, covering the
77	longest possible month so no month-to-month resizing is ever needed). Every month, the
78	manager pastes **only the code grid** (existing employee rows × day-of-month columns)
79	directly into the `1`-`31` columns, overwriting last month's codes in place —
80	`Attendance Name`/`Roster Name` aren't re-pasted or re-typed each month, since employee
81	identity doesn't change monthly. This matches "replace monthly" (confirmed earlier): the
82	table always holds exactly one month's data, never accumulates.
83	
84	## Table sizing
85	
86	Confirmed: max real department size is 11 people. Each unit table is capped at **20 data
87	rows** — comfortable margin above the real max, without being open-ended.
88	
89	## New layout
90	
91	One table per department already defined in Config's `tblSchedule` (currently PSO,
92	INFLIGHT, Admissions Office), stacked vertically, each with a 3-row gap before the next:
93	
94	```
95	Row 1      Title: "ROSTER -- paste each unit's monthly roster into its table below"
96	Row 2      (blank)
97	Row 3      "PSO ROSTER"
98	Row 4      tblRoster_PSO header: Attendance Name | Roster Name | 1 | 2 | ... | 31
99	Row 5-24   up to 20 data rows
100	Row 25-27  (blank gap)
101	Row 28     "INFLIGHT ROSTER"
102	Row 29     tblRoster_INFLIGHT header
103	Row 30-49  up to 20 data rows
104	Row 50-52  (blank gap)
105	Row 53     "ADMISSIONS OFFICE ROSTER"
106	Row 54     tblRoster_AdmissionsOffice header
107	Row 55-74  up to 20 data rows
108	```
109	
110	Every table is created with the full 33-column header (`Attendance Name`, `Roster Name`,
111	`1`-`31`) from the start — not grown incrementally as date columns get added, since the
112	headers never change after setup.
113	
114	`Attendance Name` is still filled in by hand per row — this is inherent to the
115	no-Employee-ID matching design (`2026-07-07-roster-leave-ingestion-design.md`), not
116	something a copy-paste can resolve, since the native roster doesn't carry the employee's
117	full punch-export name.
118	
119	**Table naming convention**: `tblRoster_<Department with spaces removed>` (e.g.
120	`tblRoster_AdmissionsOffice`). Adding a new department later means also adding its own
121	`tblRoster_<Dept>` table here — a manual, documented step (mirrors the existing "Adding a
122	new department" step for `tblSchedule`), not a VBA change.
123	
124	## `Helpers.LoadRoster` change
125	
126	Currently, `LoadRoster` looks for one `ListObject` named exactly `tblRoster` and discovers
127	date columns via `IsDate()`. It changes to:
128	
129	1. Iterate every `ListObject` on the Roster sheet whose name starts with `tblRoster`
130	   (prefix match) — discovery is by naming convention, not by cross-referencing
131	   `tblSchedule`'s department list. This keeps the loader simple and avoids fragile
132	   string-matching between sanitized department names and table names.
133	2. For each matching table independently: locate its `Attendance Name` column, discover
134	   its day-of-month columns (numeric `1`-`31` headers, per "Matching mechanism" above),
135	   read its rows into the same combined `rosterData` dictionary (keyed
136	   `UCase(Trim(AttendanceName)) & "|" & dayOfMonth`).
137	3. Duplicate-name and duplicate-day-column detection happens **across all tables
138	   combined** (first occurrence across all tables wins), with the warning message
139	   including which table the duplicate was found in, e.g. `"tblRoster_PSO has a
140	   duplicate Attendance Name (SYLVIA TAN) -- first occurrence used."`
141	
142	**Error-handling scope change**: today, a missing `Attendance Name` column disables
143	roster matching for the entire run. With multiple tables, this scopes down to just the
144	one broken table — a mistake in one unit's table no longer disables roster matching for
145	every other unit. A table with no `Attendance Name` column is skipped (with a warning
146	naming that table), and the loader continues to the next `tblRoster_*` table.
147	
148	If the Roster sheet has no `tblRoster*` tables at all, behavior is unchanged from today:
149	`rosterData` stays empty, every `[-]` day behaves exactly as it does without this
150	feature.
151	
152	## `ReportBuilder.bas` change
153	
154	`BuildDepartmentSheets`, `Case "NOPUNCH"` (the only place that reads `rosterData`) changes
155	its lookup key from the full date serial to the day-of-month:
156	
157	```vba
158	rKey = UCase(Trim(fName)) & "|" & Day(dayDates(d))
159	```
160	
161	(previously `UCase(Trim(fName)) & "|" & CLng(dayDates(d))`). Nothing else in this branch,
162	or any other `Case`, changes — `Clock-In Status` is still never touched by this feature,
163	and a non-match still leaves the Verification cell blank exactly as before.
164	
165	## Documentation
166	
167	- Instructions sheet: "Adding a new department" gains an optional second step —
168	  *(optional)* create a `tblRoster_<Dept>` table on the Roster sheet if you also want
169	  that department's `[-]` days auto-resolved from a roster. Skipping this step is safe;
170	  that department's `[-]` days behave exactly as they do today.
171	- `Attendance_Analyzer_Context.md` — update the Roster sheet / `tblRoster` description to
172	  describe the per-unit table structure and day-of-month matching instead of a single
173	  shared table matched by exact date.
174	
175	## Out of scope
176	
177	- No month/year tracking anywhere in the Roster sheet — day-of-month matching accepts the
178	  staleness risk described above as a process-discipline trade-off, not a gap to close in
179	  code.
180	- No automatic creation/renaming of `tblRoster_*` tables when `tblSchedule` changes —
181	  adding a department's roster table stays a manual, documented step.
182	- No support for units accumulating multiple months' data in one table (ruled out by the
183	  confirmed "replace monthly" model) — headers are permanent, only the code grid refreshes.
184	- No change to `tblRosterCodes`, the exact-match-only rule, or anything in
185	  `ReportBuilder.bas` outside the one `rKey` line above.
186	
187	## Files touched
188	
189	- `Helpers.bas` — `LoadRoster`: table discovery loop (prefix match instead of single
190	  exact name), day-of-month column discovery (numeric `1`-`31` instead of `IsDate()`),
191	  per-table error scoping, warning messages naming the source table.
192	- `ReportBuilder.bas` — `BuildDepartmentSheets`, `Case "NOPUNCH"`: `rKey` built from
193	  `Day(dayDates(d))` instead of `CLng(dayDates(d))`.
194	- `Attendance_All_Modules.txt` (regenerated via `./regen_modules.ps1` after source edits,
195	  per the dual-source maintenance convention in `CLAUDE.md`)
196	- `Attendance_Analyzer_Context.md` — document the per-unit Roster table structure and
197	  day-of-month matching.
198	- `Attendance_Analyzer.xlsx` (tracked in this repo) — Roster sheet rebuilt into the
199	  per-unit stacked layout above, each table created with the full static
200	  `Attendance Name | Roster Name | 1..31` header (`tblRoster_PSO`, `tblRoster_INFLIGHT`,
201	  `tblRoster_AdmissionsOffice`, replacing the single `tblRoster` table); Instructions
202	  sheet gets the new optional step.

3	## Purpose
4	Monthly macro tool for TTSH ICH PSO team. Managers export a "Monthly Punch List" report
5	from the ZKBio CVAccess attendance system, run a macro against it, and get back an Excel
6	workbook with attendance flagged by department (late, missing punches, no-punch days that
7	need manual verification, hours worked vs expected).
8	
9	## Ideal state / target use case (user's vision, confirmed 2026-07-08)
10	The ZKBio CVAccess biometric scanner is used by **everyone in TTSH**, so the end goal is a
11	tool **any TTSH department can adopt** — potentially the user's most-used and most important
12	project — not just ICH PSO. See
13	`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-08-ttsh-wide-adoption-design.md` for the approved design.
14	The pillars:
15	
16	1. **Verbatim copy-paste config, never transcription.** The punchlist format is stable
17	   across departments; only names and department strings vary. Managers paste those strings
18	   verbatim from their own punchlist into Config/Roster, so exact-match joins can't fail.
19	   The person join key is the punchlist's single name column (col B) — the Last Name column
20	   is always empty in real exports.
21	2. **Maximum Config-sheet flexibility, zero VBA for managers.** Everything a department
22	   needs to tune (schedules, grace period, hours unit, verification options, roster codes)
23	   lives in editable Config tables. Pre-provisioned blank department slots (generic
24	   `tblRoster_DeptN` tables with the department name typed *inside* the table, blank
25	   schedule rows) mean managers never create, rename, or resize an Excel Table — but
26	   nothing so dynamic that the code becomes undebuggable.
27	3. **Roster paste tolerance.** Managers paste their whole roster grid verbatim — colours,
28	   fonts, and stray rows are inert (loader reads values only); unknown codes are reported
29	   in end-of-run warnings, never silently dropped.
30	4. **Pre-run validation.** Before building sheets, the run reports punchlist names missing
31	   from the roster, departments missing from `tblSchedule`, and stale roster names — silent
32	   mismatch is impossible.
33	5. **Per-department distribution.** Each department's export contains only its own people,
34	   so each department gets its own configured copy of the `.xlsm`, cloned from a master
35	   template the user maintains. No shared workbook.
36	6. **Output = overview + depth.** One output workbook per run: an Overview landing sheet
37	   (headline numbers per unit, hyperlinks to detail) plus the existing per-department
38	   day-by-day sheets with per-employee summary blocks. Weekday/date matching stays derived
39	   automatically from the punchlist headers (`ParseDayHeaders`).
40	
41	**This has NOT been run in live Excel/VBA.** It was written and logic-checked by porting the
42	same rules to Python and running them against a real punch export, but the VBA itself is
43	untested. Treat first-run debugging as expected, not a sign something is fundamentally wrong.

## Summary: Implementation status of the 6 design-spec items

**1. Name matching (join key = col B alone) — NOT DONE**
`ReportBuilder.bas` line 161 still builds the join key from *both* First and Last Name columns: `fName = Trim(Trim(srcWs.Cells(r,2).Value) & " " & Trim(srcWs.Cells(r,3).Value))`. This same `fName` is used as the roster lookup key (line 237: `rKey = UCase(Trim(fName)) & "|" & Day(dayDates(d))`). The spec's "col B alone, verbatim paste" design is only described in `Attendance_Analyzer_Context.md` lines 18-20 as the *target* state — code hasn't changed.

**2. Pre-run validation — NOT DONE**
`MainMacro.GenerateAttendanceReport` (lines 24-40) has exactly the same 4 pipeline steps as before the spec (LoadConfig → LoadRoster → ParseDayHeaders → BuildDepartmentSheets). No validation pass exists anywhere for punchlist-names-missing-from-roster, punchlist-depts-missing-from-tblSchedule, or roster-names-never-in-punchlist. `Attendance_Analyzer_Context.md` line 30-32 describes this as a design pillar, but it's aspirational text, not implemented behavior.

**3. Config pre-provisioned blank department slots — NOT DONE**
`Helpers.LoadRoster` (lines 168-276) discovers tables by name prefix only (`UCase(Left(lo.Name,9)) <> "TBLROSTER"`, line 205) and never reads a department-name cell from inside the table region — this matches the earlier `2026-07-07-roster-per-unit-tables-design.md` (dept-named tables like `tblRoster_PSO`), not the new spec's generic `tblRoster_Dept1..N` + in-table department cell. `tblSchedule` blank rows would already work mechanically (LoadConfig loops over all rows regardless of content), but the roster half of item 3 requires a code change that hasn't happened.

**4. Roster paste tolerance hardening — PARTIALLY DONE**
Already true and confirmed in code: reads `.Value` only (Helpers.bas lines 251, 262), case-insensitive/trimmed code matching (lines 184, 239-240, 251, 262), blank/stray rows inert (line 252 `If empName = "" Then GoTo NextRosterRow`). NOT done: "unknown codes reported only for unresolved `[-]` days" — there is no code anywhere (checked `ReportBuilder.bas`, `Helpers.bas`) that adds an unrecognized-code warning to `RosterWarnings`. `RosterWarnings` only ever records missing-column/duplicate-name/duplicate-day/unexpected-error cases (Helpers.bas lines 215, 235, 255, 272), never "code found but not in tblRosterCodes."

**5. Distribution (one workbook per dept, master template) — NOT DONE**
No code exists for this (expected, since it's a workflow/process item), and no scripting/tooling for cloning per-department `.xlsm` copies was found anywhere in the repo.

**6. Overview sheet — NOT DONE**
No "Overview" sheet creation code exists in `ReportBuilder.bas` or `MainMacro.bas`. The output workbook (`MainMacro.bas` line 39, `Workbooks.Add`) only ever gets per-department sheets plus "Unmapped" (`ReportBuilder.BuildDepartmentSheets`, lines 170-194) — no landing/summary sheet, no hyperlinks.

**Net assessment:** All 6 items are still in the "documented vision" stage (`Attendance_Analyzer_Context.md` "Ideal state" section, confirmed 2026-07-08) rather than implemented. The only genuinely-shipped prior work is the per-unit roster table + day-of-month matching design (2026-07-07 specs), which items 3 and 4 partially build on but haven't yet extended.
